thread:
amanda: Heads-up — we've had a few support tickets asking why org X can hit the hosted API for small models but is immediately rate-limited on the L-3 family. Are we doing model-specific quotas anywhere today or is it just global per-org buckets?
kevin: Today it's just global per-org + per-key burst allowance. No per-model differentiation.
sri: FWIW we have model metadata (family/size) in the routing layer. Could enforce at ingress if we add per-family weight multipliers.
amanda: Sounds reasonable. Two big questions: 1) how do we count requests (tokens vs requests vs peak concurrency), and 2) how to support bursts for premium customers?
jon: Counting: token-weighted quotas make the most sense long-term — bigger models cost more on backend. But token accounting is tricky with streaming and early-abort.
maria: Also UX: customers expect to see "limits by model" on the console. If we add per-family limits, we need a clear display and an override flow for Dedicated/Enterprise.
kevin: Implementation options: 
- Option A: per-org token budget, but each model family has a multiplier (e.g., gpt-small x1, gpt-medium x2, gpt-large x4). Enforcement done at admission using request token_estimate * multiplier.
- Option B: separate buckets per-family per-org (independent counters). Easier to surface on UI but multiplies state.
- Option C: hybrid — global token pool + per-family burst windows.
sri: I prefer A for storage simplicity; admission needs token_estimate though. We already have a fast token estimator used by our cost-affinity router. Can reuse it.
amanda: Burst behaviour? Customers want short bursts for sudden spikes (e.g., chat replays). We should support a token burst bucket that refreshes faster for higher tiers.
jon: We must ensure fairness across keys. If we allow per-key bursts on top of per-org buckets we could be gamed: many keys -> effective higher capacity.
kevin: enforce per-org golden rule: limit burst consumption aggregated at org level. Keys can reserve small local burst but capped by org remaining burst allowance.
maria: For console: mockup idea — show a stacked bar: global org quota, per-family consumption overlay, and a small "burst credit" meter. Click-through shows policy and override button (Enterprise only).
sri: API change: router needs model_family in header if not derivable from request: `X-Model-Family: gpt-large`. Also store `x-estimated-input-tokens` and `x-estimated-output-tokens` for telemetry.
kevin: telemetry plan: emit metrics: `quota.consumed.tokens`, tags: org_id, model_family, key_id, billing_tier. Also `quota.burst.used` and `quota.denied` with denial_reason.
deploy-bot: Document updated: https://internal.redwood/doc/quota-modeling — new section on "Family-weighted quotas" (edited by s_r_).
amanda: Proposal: adopt Option A (multiplier on token estimator) + org-level burst bucket. Enforcement at ingress gateway for fast rejection, with advisory warnings from scheduler if close to limit. Rollout: feature-flagged canary (10% of traffic) -> 50% -> 100%.
jon: For canary we should use low-risk orgs and synthetic traffic that exercises streaming paths. Add regression tests for streaming early-cancel token refunds.
maria: I'll prototype the console panel and the tooltip copy. Will hand off a Figma by EOD Thursday.
kevin: I'll add telemetry counters and a quick Grafana dashboard for the canary. Suggest `eng-platform/quota-family-canary` dashboard.
amanda: I'll own the RFC and roll plan. Action items:
- amanda: RFC + rollout timeline (due Tue)
- sri: router admission changes + estimator reuse (PR target: next sprint)
- kevin: telemetry + Grafana (canary dashboards)
- maria: console mockups + copy (Figma by Thu)
- jon: canary test harness and streaming regression tests
We'll keep feature-flagged until all telemetry and UI are in place. Thanks :thumbsup:
kevin: quick Q — should we include embeddings models in the same family weighting or have separate rules? embeddings are tiny per-token but sometimes huge volumes.
sri: separate profile for embeddings makes sense — smaller multiplier but different billing tag. We'll add `model_profile: embedding` and allow policy per-profile.
amanda: Great catch. Let's sync tomorrow 10am to finalize multipliers.
kevin: +1
jon: +1
maria: +1 :sparkles:
